source_spans.locator: Annual Review of Psychology 68 (2017), published pp.101-103, abstract/introduction: high-dimensional continuous partially observed states, sparse data, and long-range action-outcome dependencies motivate retaining individual-event information as a possible partial computational remedy

Annual Review of Psychology 68 (2017), published pp.109-113, nonparametric-value and formalization sections plus Figure 1: individual event/trajectory records are retained, retrieved at choice time, weighted by similarity to the current state, and combined into state or state-action value estimates

Annual Review of Psychology 68 (2017), published pp.113-119, empirical and computational discussion: direct empirical support is sparse; kernel generalization, state-space structure, low-data conditions, and bias-variance trade-offs constrain the proposal

Annual Review of Psychology 68 (2017), published p.123, Conclusions: the proposed additional learning system is a partial solution to complex sparse long-range problems, but the theory is explicitly described as still largely speculative and in need of more precise formalization

conditions: decision problems with high-dimensional, continuous, or partially observed states
sparse experience in which the same state may rarely or never recur exactly
sequential problems containing dependencies between actions and outcomes over temporal distances that can violate simple Markov assumptions
task: estimate state or state-action return at choice time and compare candidate action values
temporal_scope: individual experienced trajectories retain sequential information across their stored duration
retrieval and similarity-based weighting occur at choice time rather than requiring the relevant generalization rule to be fixed at initial encoding

nodes.description: retained record of an individual experienced event or trajectory linking multiple features and sequential elements together with its associated return
current state at which candidate actions are being evaluated
choice-time weighting rule that assigns greater influence to retained traces according to their similarity to the current state or corresponding state-action query
retained prior trajectories retrieved for the current decision and weighted by the declared similarity rule
nonparametric estimate of expected future return for a state or state-action alternative constructed from retained trace returns
choice among candidate actions obtained by comparing their estimated returns

relations.description: at choice time, retained event traces are retrieved and weighted according to their similarity to the current decision state rather than being replaced at encoding by one fixed aggregate summary
the weighted returns associated with retrieved traces are combined to form a nonparametric estimate of state or state-action return
comparison of the resulting return estimates across candidate actions supplies the decision variable used to derive a choice policy

a stored trajectory directly preserves dependencies only across its finite recorded duration; estimating consequences beyond that duration requires additional chaining or value information and may invoke further assumptions
